item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J01270","case1_error":"Uses water remaining instead of water lost to count jumps, then unjustifiably subtracts the count from itself.","case2_error":"Incorrectly sets Sam's money equal to Giselle's minus $15, misassigning the stated comparison between Isabella and Giselle.","reason":"The first confuses remaining volume with allowable loss and introduces self-subtraction; the second attaches a monetary comparison to the wrong people.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01271","case1_error":"Uses 12 birds per snake instead of the stated 3, substituting the beetle consumption rate into the wrong relationship.","case2_error":"Gives an unsupported final 40% after stating the correct percentage formula; the correct result is 20%.","reason":"The first explicitly uses an incorrect rate. The second states a correct formula but supplies an incorrect number without showing its calculation.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01272","case1_error":"Invents an initial zero-cookie inventory and updates it inconsistently with removals, ignoring the two returned cookies.","case2_error":"Assigns all 60 remaining cupcakes to each flavor, doubling the remainder, and falsely claims 60 is its only even divisor.","reason":"The first fabricates and inconsistently tracks inventory; the second duplicates a total that must be divided between two flavors.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01273","case1_error":"After correct group expressions, introduces unsupported numerical totals and an extra addend of 64, producing 112 instead of 40.","case2_error":"Subtracts the parent-child age difference from the parents' current age instead of subtracting Mark's age.","reason":"The first introduces unsupported totals and an additional summand; the second explicitly uses the wrong age relationship despite already calculating the requested age.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J01274","case1_error":"Subtracts car expenses from the console price instead of subtracting remaining savings, ignoring the calculated earnings when determining the shortfall.","case2_error":"Multiplies the combined bedroom time by three again for the living room and divides work among four people instead of three.","reason":"The first misrepresents spending as progress toward the purchase; the second repeats an aggregation factor and miscounts workers.","judgment":"different"}]}
